title: Turn interviews into a product decision
desc: For a researcher or product manager with notes but no agreed next move.
inputs: Interview notes or transcripts, who attended each one, the research question, the decision you need to make and any scoring inputs you have, such as reach, impact, confidence and effort for RICE.
prompt: Use these interview notes to identify supported needs, write job statements from them, and rank which problems deserve investigation next.
outcome: Findings tied to source passages, job statements, and a ranked list of problems with each score’s formula and any unsourced input flagged.

steps.why: Extract findings, pain points and exact quotes from the interviews, with each speaker named.
Write job statements from the struggling moments and hire and fire criteria in those findings.
Rank the resulting problems with one named scoring method, such as RICE or Opportunity Score.

note: If you only have internal opinions, use them as hypotheses. They cannot stand in for interview findings.

title: Make a feature idea ready to discuss with engineers
desc: For a product owner, founder or designer who needs behavior defined before implementation.
inputs: The product’s brief or folder, the user problem, existing behavior and constraints, any research or support evidence, and other planned work if sequencing matters.
prompt: Turn this feature idea into a specification with user flows, requirements and testable acceptance criteria. Identify the decisions we still need to make, and if sequencing matters, show the feature on a roadmap beside its dependencies.
outcome: A feature specification for the release decision it serves, with user flows, requirements, testable acceptance criteria and the decisions still open, and a roadmap when sequencing matters.

steps.why: Check the current product evidence and identify the release decision the feature serves.
Turn the evidence and release decision into user flows, requirements and acceptance criteria.
If sequencing is part of the decision, show the feature alongside dependencies and other planned work.

note: A small, well-understood change can start at Write feature spec.

title: Fix a website people cannot find their way around
desc: For a designer, founder or content owner who decides the site’s navigation and labels.
inputs: The site’s URL, its sitemap or page inventory, the main visitor tasks, and any search or usability observations.
prompt: Review this site against the tasks visitors need to complete. Propose clearer navigation and labels, prepare a usability study to test the changes, and check the navigation for accessibility barriers.
outcome: A proposed site structure, the reasons behind its labels, participant tasks that test whether people find the right content, and accessibility findings with proposed repairs.

steps.why: Compare the content structure with visitor tasks and propose navigation and labels.
Turn the risky navigation assumptions into neutral participant tasks.
Check the site against WCAG 2.2 AA for barriers that keep people from using the navigation.

note: Usability findings require actual participant observations; an agent walkthrough is not a substitute.

title: Find the gaps in an everyday business process
desc: For an operations lead improving approvals, onboarding or another recurring process.
inputs: An existing SOP, staff notes, forms, system exports or a description of what happens today, any durations, costs or team estimates you have for scoring changes, and touchpoints or research on the experience of the people involved.
prompt: Map how this process currently works, including triggers, owners, systems and exceptions. Show the handoffs that need clarification, map the experience of the customers or staff involved where they feel its delays or errors, and propose changes ranked with one named scoring method.
outcome: A map of the current process, unresolved ownership questions, a journey map and service blueprint where customers or staff feel those delays or errors, and ranked changes with any guessed score flagged.

steps.why: Document the actual steps and exceptions, or use Optimize mode to find where the process loses time, money or quality.
When a customer’s or staff member’s experience is part of the gap, connect those steps to the people involved and the systems supporting them.
Rank the proposed changes with one named scoring method, such as RICE or a weighted decision matrix.

note: Design process alone is enough for an SOP. For a sales process spread across CRM exports and discovery files, use Map sales process instead.

title: Plan a sprint that fits the team’s capacity
desc: For a team lead or product owner with more backlog than capacity.
inputs: The Requirements tab from Capture requirements, team estimates and availability, recent velocity, the RAID log, and the definitions of ready and done; the decision log and each week’s meeting notes once the sprint starts.
prompt: Review this backlog for readiness, propose a sprint goal with commit and stretch work that fits our available capacity, then track the sprint’s status, risks and decisions.
outcome: Readiness gaps, a sprint goal and a proposed commit and stretch split sized to the team’s capacity, then a weekly status report and RAID and decision log entries during the sprint.

steps.why: Identify unclear, oversized or blocked items before selecting the sprint.
Size the commitment against each person’s available capacity and the sprint goal.
During delivery, record status, risks and decisions in the weekly status report and the RAID and decision logs.

note: If estimates or capacity are missing, the team supplies them before Claude proposes a commitment.

title: Start and validate a signed client project
desc: For a project manager receiving work from a sales or account team.
inputs: The executed statement of work, its quote, the deal record and the receiving delivery owner; the requirements workbook and Test Plan once testing starts.
prompt: Build the handoff package for this signed project so the receiving owner can accept it. Once it is accepted, draft the charter, kickoff decks and Sprint 0 plan, and later the test scripts, UAT tracker and defect log.
outcome: A handoff package, a draft charter with RAID and decision logs, kickoff decks, a Sprint 0 plan, test scripts traced to the requirements, a UAT tracker and a defect log.

steps.why: Build the handoff package from the executed statement of work, quote and deal record, with every gap given a named owner.
Draft the charter, kickoff decks and Sprint 0 plan from the accepted handoff, restating the executed statement of work’s scope without renegotiating it.
Use the requirements workbook and Test Plan to build test scripts traced to each requirement, a UAT tracker and a defect log.

note: Run each step when the project reaches it, starting with the handoff at signature.

title: Develop or review a Salesforce change
desc: For a developer working on Apex, triggers or LWC in an existing repository.
inputs: The repository with its Apex and LWC files, its architecture decisions, the GitHub issue for the change and the confirmed target org.
prompt: Write or review this Salesforce change against the project’s architecture decisions. Keep business logic reusable across entry points, explain design issues, run local checks and a dry run against the confirmed org, then merge and deploy once I authorize it.
outcome: A code change or specific review findings, architecture-check results, and validation and deployment evidence.

steps.why: Read the project’s architecture decisions, then write or review code in the trigger, service, selector, unit-of-work and controller layers, and run the architecture checker.
On a single-org project, work from the change’s GitHub issue in an isolated worktree, run local checks and a dry run against the confirmed org, then squash-merge and deploy from main.

note: Configure Salesforce project is a separate option when you want to install or repair delivery standards and Claude hooks; do not run it just to review code.

title: Set up, audit or repair a Salesforce repository’s Claude hooks
desc: For a maintainer whose hooks stopped running, whose tracker or trunk branch changed, or whose team is adopting delivery standards.
inputs: The Salesforce repository with any existing hooks and its CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, the intended tracker, trunk branch, host and ownership mode, the team’s architecture decisions, one real Apex or LWC change, and authentication already set up.
prompt: Audit this Salesforce repository’s delivery standards and Claude hooks and explain the gaps. Install or repair only what I approve, preserve working configuration and run the architecture checker on one real change.
outcome: A standards audit, or hooks and a CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md block installed or repaired and checked to confirm each is armed, plus architecture-check results.

steps.why: Run the prerequisites check, then install, audit or repair the hooks and the managed CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md block.
Run the architecture checker on a real Apex or LWC change and report what it flags.

note: Choose audit while the team is still deciding whether to adopt these standards: a plain audit changes nothing. A repository configuration change does not authorize a deployment to a Salesforce org.

title: Run an existing Salesforce release pipeline
desc: For a release owner operating a repository that already uses sf-deploy-engine.
inputs: The repository with its pipeline.yml, the engine token already stored privately, the target environment and the tickets or commit SHAs to move.
prompt: Check the configured Salesforce pipeline and target environment, then run the validation, promotion, release or rollback I authorize and report the evidence and any blockers.
outcome: Engine status and the verified result of the requested operation, or the blocker that stopped it.

steps.why: Report status from pipeline.yml and run the authorized operation through the engine instead of a manual sf deploy.

note: A team on Salesforce DevOps Center uses Manage Salesforce DevOps in its promotion mode instead.

title: Prepare a prospect call and find the offering that fits
desc: For a seller or consultant with an account to research and a call coming up.
inputs: The account context, prior discovery notes, the attendee list, your offering catalog with its qualifiers and the decision the next call should advance; after the call, its notes or transcript.
prompt: Use this account context and discovery evidence to prepare the next call and identify the open questions. After the call, turn my notes into findings and rank which offering in my catalog fits, citing the evidence for each point.
outcome: A call brief with ranked questions, then findings from the call, a ranked offering fit with the evidence behind each score, and the open questions.

steps.why: Use the account context to update the pursuit brief or prepare one upcoming call with an objective, agenda and ranked questions.
Turn the call notes into supported findings and open questions.
Score the findings against each offering’s qualifiers and rank the fit, citing the evidence for each point.

note: Without the qualifiers, the offering fit is diagnostic only.

title: Compare scope options before writing a statement of work
desc: For a consultant or account lead choosing what to include in a proposal.
inputs: The project brief and constraints, comparable past work, your rate card, a versioned quote export, and your approved contract profile.
prompt: Develop and compare these scope options. Explain inclusions, exclusions, effort and tradeoffs, then draft the statement of work for the option I choose from the confirmed quote and contract profile.
outcome: A side-by-side comparison of the options and, once you confirm the choice and contract profile, a draft statement of work in Word.

steps.why: Build each option’s scope items with effort and staffing estimates, leaving work with no effort basis unestimated.
Reconcile each option’s scope items, hours, staffing and price from one quote revision into one HTML side-by-side comparison.
Render the confirmed quote revision and your approved contract profile as a Word statement of work once its hours and revenue tie out.

note: Run Review deal economics before the statement of work if the quote needs internal margin approval.

title: Prepare an application for a specific role
desc: For a job seeker tailoring a resume and cover letter to one posting from their own career evidence.
inputs: The job posting, career evidence, current resume, your criteria for the role and pay thresholds, and your confirmed writing profile for the drafts.
prompt: Assess this role against my criteria and pay thresholds, then prepare the application. Tailor my resume and supporting materials using only the experience and results my sources support.
outcome: A role assessment, role work record, tailored resume and drafts of the cover letter or other supporting materials you request.

steps.why: Compare the role’s pay, scope and progression with your criteria and pay thresholds, keeping unknown terms as questions.
Build the role work record, matching the posting’s requirements to your career evidence.
Rewrite the resume bullets for this posting, placing its keywords where they describe supported work and checking each figure against your career evidence.
Draft the cover letter, outreach or form answers you request from the role work record, keeping facts consistent with the tailored resume.

note: Prepare job application holds the Tailor resume and Draft application materials modes. Claude does not submit an application without your explicit authorization.

title: Turn a project into a portfolio case study
desc: For a designer, product professional or consultant explaining their own work.
inputs: The project evidence, your contribution and decisions, approved outcomes, publication or confidentiality constraints, your case-study template and a confirmed writing profile.
prompt: Turn this project into a case study that explains the problem, what I did and decided, and what the work made possible. Identify anything that needs permission before publication.
outcome: A working copy with evidence labels on every figure and a clean publish copy, with open permission questions listed.

steps.why: Bracket missing facts in the working copy instead of filling them, then check the publish gates, including sanitization and ownership, before the publish copy is called ready.
Review the publish copy against your writing rules, keeping every figure and quotation exact.

note: Use Develop independent product first only if you want to create a company-neutral product or offer from historical work.

title: Improve a draft without losing its meaning
desc: For anyone revising a document, reply, instructions or interface text who must keep its facts and voice.
inputs: The draft, intended reader, purpose, required facts and your writing rules folder, if you keep one.
prompt: Review this draft for clarity and repetition. Preserve its meaning, qualifications and voice, flag any claim the required facts do not support, and return the complete revision.
outcome: The complete revised draft, with quotations and figures kept exact and unsupported claims identified.

steps.why: Read the whole draft for meaning and structure and repair vague or repetitive passages.

note: Use Manage writing profile only to build or revise a person’s profile from writing they have authorized you to use.

title: Build a deck that supports a decision
desc: For a team lead, founder or consultant preparing a pitch, proposal or briefing that asks an audience to decide.
inputs: The audience, the decision, your sources, supported numbers, the format you need (PowerPoint or HTML) and any confirmed brand.
prompt: Build a briefing deck for this audience and decision. Use these sources to explain the options and recommendation, with visuals that clarify the argument, then review the finished deck before release.
outcome: An editable deck with reviewed copy and explanatory visuals, plus a release decision that lists any required repairs.

steps.why: Set a one-sentence thesis and slide structure from the audience decision and sources, then build the editable deck.
Check the finished deck against the sources, requested task, writing and rendered format.

note: With no confirmed brand, the deck uses the neutral profile, which has system fonts and no logo.

title: Take a sticker idea through design and sheet layout
desc: For a maker developing typography-led stickers for printing.
inputs: The message, intended size, visual references and production constraints; later, the approved PNGs, how many of each you need and your project’s sheet generator.
prompt: Explore distinct sticker compositions for this message and size. Once I choose a design and supply the approved PNGs, lay them out as Cricut Print Then Cut sheets.
outcome: Compositions and print-scale proofs, then Print Then Cut sheets checked for every requested count and DPI.

steps.why: Show structurally different compositions, audition your words in real font files and critique them at print scale before settling on artwork.
Lay out the supplied PNGs with the sheet generator, confirming paper size separately from the cut area.

note: If the sheet generator is missing, Claude asks for it instead of guessing. The sheets still need a physical alignment and print test.

title: Answer a game question from your own planner
desc: For a Fortune’s Weave player checking a route, roster or planning decision.
inputs: The planner project location, or an export of its current roster and route, plus the question you want answered.
prompt: Use my current Fortune’s Weave planner to answer this question. Separate what the game sources establish from any planning recommendation, and propose a planner update if needed.
outcome: A sourced answer, or a planner update made with your approval and then verified.

steps.why: Read the live roster, planner state and only the researched section the question needs before recommending a team or changing a build.

title: Resume a project after a break
desc: For someone returning to an ongoing project or handing it to another session.
inputs: The project name, the result you want next, and its source folder or authorized hub connection.
prompt: Find the current project state and controlling sources. Explain what is complete, what is open and the next action the sources support, then prepare a handoff another session can use.
outcome: The project’s current context, any conflicting records, the next action and a handoff another session can resume from.

steps.why: Read the project’s index of records and the records this work needs, then name any source conflicts and the next supported action.
Write a handoff from the context Step 1 found, with the current state, open questions and exact next action.

note: Without a hub connection, Claude works from files you supply and names what it could not check.

title: Package a repeated workflow as a reusable skill
desc: For someone adding a workflow to their own Skills Estate checkout.
inputs: The repeated task and how you do it now, example requests, expected outputs, known failure cases, your Skills Estate checkout and the target host.
prompt: Check whether an existing skill already covers this workflow; if not, turn it into a skill with focused triggers, intake, examples and failure behavior. Review the draft for release, then build and inspect its package for the target host.
outcome: A draft skill with its intake, required resources and test results, a release decision with any required repairs, and an inspected package for the target host.

steps.why: Check the closest existing skills for overlap, record the intake, then scaffold a draft and test it on a positive, an alternate and a nearby negative request.
Check the draft skill against the request and its sources, and return a release decision with any required repairs.
Build the package for the target host and inspect its archive hash and contents before anything is installed.

note: Install Maintain skills estate, which holds the authoring and release modes.
